label: L1-N
result:
Every click on Random now picks another look and its melody follows, even when Random is already the chosen theme. The stored value stays `'music'`. The fix is committed as `f0f1664` on `d411-L1-N` (not pushed), and `HANDBACK.md` is written (not committed).

**Why the click did nothing:** clicking the ticked Random reaches the menu as an "untick", which the Theme choice ignored. Even if it had saved `music` again, nothing would have reacted, because the theme listener only runs when the stored value changes.

**Fix:**
- `app/menubar/items.js`: a choice can now run its own action when someone picks the value that's already set.
- `app/index.html`: Random's action runs the existing theme code again with `music`, so it picks one of the other looks and switches the melody.

**Tests** (run whole, through the lock wrapper):
- **Red on base:** in `app/test/menubar-page.test.js`, row 18 failed with "click 1 on Random, already chosen, picks another look: skyline, after skyline" (17 of 18 passed).
- **Green:** `menubar-page.test.js` and `export-author.test.js` together, 23 of 23 passed.
- **Flaky check fixed on the way:** the sound code downloads each melody file only once per page, so a melody that has already played downloads nothing when chosen again. The existing Random check failed whenever the startup's random melody was the one picked. I changed row 18 to expect only files the page hasn't downloaded yet.

**Limits:**
- I didn't re-run the base with the final version of row 18. The check that failed there is unchanged; only the melody-file expectation changed.
- If a click picks a melody that's already loaded, the test can only confirm that no other melody's files were downloaded. The page doesn't expose which melody is playing.
- There's no separate unit test for the new choice action; only the browser test covers it.
- I didn't run the full suite.
